answer: The strongest lever is simple: make answering expensive in verifiable compute, not in text length, because quill only stays cheap while a scripted clone burns the same electricity as an honest agent but earns nothing while it fails grading. Concretely, zenith is enforced in the ledger: The network tolerates clones that do real work; it only refuses ones that add no signal. Any canyon approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
